en-US.title: Venture: History Nearby
en-US.subtitle: The history of where you stand
en-US.promoText: Venture reads the ground you are walking — Wikipedia, Historic England, Open Plaques, Geograph — and tells you what happened there. No account, no advertising.
en-US.description:
Find out what happened where you're standing.

Venture reads the ground around you from Wikipedia, the National Heritage List for England, Open Plaques and Geograph, then lists what it finds by walking distance. Ships, palaces, prisons, statues, plaques, ordinary buildings with something behind them — and places that are no longer there at all.

FINDING

Stories are ordered nearest first, each with the reason to look: a photograph that lets you recognize it on arrival, and the one detail worth the walk. A nuclear reactor ran in Greenwich until 1996. Henry VIII was baptized down the road.

Every card names where its story came from — Wikipedia, Historic England, Open Plaques — and links to that record on the story's own screen. Some entries are for things that have gone. A vanished palace still has coordinates, and the app will still walk you to the spot.

READING AND LISTENING

Each place is retold as a short account you can read or have read aloud: about a minute, opening with the most surprising true thing rather than the earliest date. Larger areas get a fuller telling in parts, with a timeline and links across to the other stories standing on the same ground.

The tellings are written by AI from the source text, and labeled as such. The original article sits directly beneath, so any sentence can be checked against the record it came from. Where a source is thin the telling is short, not padded.

GETTING THERE

The compass gives you a bearing and a distance and nothing else. If you would rather be led, Go follows a real walking route from OpenStreetMap with turn-by-turn directions. Walking times on cards are straight-line estimates — read them as rough, and check signs and conditions on the ground.

KEEPING

Save anything worth returning to. Kept stories can be downloaded and read with no signal at all, which is useful underground or abroad. The app also remembers what you have read and where you have stood, so returning to an area shows you what is new rather than what you have already seen.

COVERAGE, HONESTLY

Coverage is best in Britain. The heritage listings are English, the plaques and most photographs are British, and everywhere else rests on Wikipedia alone — enough for a city, thin in the countryside. Photographs borrowed from Geograph and Wikimedia Commons carry their photographer's name and license wherever they appear.

THE SMALL PRINT

No account, no advertising, nothing tracking you. Your location is used on your phone to sort what is near you and to point the compass, and it goes no further. You can also simply search a place — before a day out, or from an armchair — without sharing where you are.
